observation.visible_scene: An indoor swimming pool viewed from a water-level camera at the near end; a dark lane line runs down the center of the pool toward the far wall, and a small portion of a limb (knee/foot) is visible at the bottom edge of the frame. At the far end, a shirtless person in dark trunks treads water while handling two white ball-like objects. The background (tiled wall, round clock, red alarm, ventilation pipes, a rack holding rows of white items, and a colorful umbrella-like object on the left) stays fixed in position throughout.
visible_changes: The person at the far end remains centered at the end of the lane line with no net translation along the pool; only their arms, torso, and the white objects move.

For most of the excerpt the person holds one white object at chest level while repeatedly raising the other white object above their head (e.g., frames 3-8, 18-30, 37-41), then lowering it again (frames 13-17, 31-36).
Around frames 9-12 the person bends their torso forward and lowers the white object(s) toward the water surface, then straightens back up.
Splashing and disturbed water appear around the person's body during the arm motions and the forward lean (e.g., frames 1, 13-17, 35-36).

The water surface ripples and the dark lane line shifts slightly in apparent shape due to surface motion, while the wall and clock remain stationary, indicating the camera itself is essentially static (at most minor bobbing).
Bright patches on the water are surface reflections of overhead light, not separate objects.
outside_clip_unknowns: The purpose of the activity (drill, game, or exercise) and whether the white objects are thrown to or received from the camera person is not shown.
What happens before frame 1 and after frame 41, including any landing, release, or completion of the object handling, is outside the excerpt.
The exact identity of the white objects (balls, floats, or paddles) and the meaning of the forward lean (scooping vs. placing) cannot be confirmed from these frames alone.
uncertain_details: Whether the raised white object is being tossed and caught or simply lifted and held is ambiguous.
The slight apparent wiggle of the lane line is water-surface motion, not camera translation; camera movement is minimal/uncertain.
The person's body position relative to the lane-line end is essentially constant; perceived shifts are due to posture changes, not locomotion.
